Text: At noon she found dinner ready, and while at table, was entertained with an excellent concert of music, though without seeing any body

cont_1.Text: but at night, as she was going to sit down to supper, she heard the noise Beast made; and could not help being sadly terrified.

cont_2.Text: Sophia, will you give me leave to see you sup?

cont_4.Text: No, you alone are mistress here; you need only bid me be gone, if my presence is troublesome, and I will immediately withdraw: but tell me, do not you think me very ugly?

cont_5.Text: That is true, for I cannot tell a lie; but I believe you are very good-natured.

cont_6.Text: So I am, but then, besides my ugliness, I have no sense; I know very well that I am a poor, silly, stupid creature.

cont_7.Text: Tis no sign of folly to think so, for never did fool know this, or had so humble a conceit of his own understanding.

cont_8.Text: Eat then, Sophia, and endeavour to amuse yourself in your palace; for every thing here is yours, and I should be very uneasy if you were not happy.

cont_9.Text: You are very obliging, I own I am pleased with your kindness, and when I consider that, your deformity scarce appears.

cont_10.Text: Yes, yes, my heart is good, but still I am a monster.

cont_11.Text: Among mankind, there are many that deserve that name more than you, and I prefer you, just as your are, to those, who, under a human form, hide a treacherous, corrupt, and ungrateful heart.

cont_12.Text: If I had sense enough, I would make a fine compliment to thank you, but I am so dull, that I can only say, I am greatly obliged to you.

cont_13.Text: Sophia ate a hearty supper, and had almost conquered her dread of the monster. But then she nearly dropped her fork, when suddenly the Beast spoke.

cont_14.Text: Sophia, will you be my wife?

cont_15.Text: She was some time before she durst answer; for she was afraid of making him angry, if she refused. At last, however, she said, trembling,

cont_18.Text: He left the room; and only turned back, now and then, to look at her as he went out. When Sophia was alone, she felt a great deal of compassion for poor Beast.

cont_19.Text: Alas, 'tis a thousand pities any thing so good-natured should be so ugly.
